messages.subject: Group operations
parts:
Is there some nice way of using plyr to perform operations on the groups defined by the grouping variable, e.g. sort the groups or take a subset of the group?

Of course, these operations are easy enough to perform using base ddply:

test <- data.frame( a = rep(1:3,1:3), b = 1:6)

Order groups by decreasing length of group:

     arrange(ddply(test,.(a),mutate,key=length(a)),desc(key))[,-3]   # the "-3" for removing the temp key column is particularly ugly

Select groups with an odd size (like 'having' in SQL):

     ddply(test,.(a),function(d) if (nrow(d)%%2 == 1) d)

... but I was thinking something like this could be a useful standard facility.

              -s

messages.subject: Re: Group operations

On Fri, May 20, 2011 at 4:56 PM, Stavros Macrakis <macr...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> Is there some nice way of using plyr to perform operations on the
> groups defined by the grouping variable, e.g. sort the groups or take a
> subset of the group?
> Of course, these operations are easy enough to perform using base ddply:
> test <- data.frame( a = rep(1:3,1:3), b = 1:6)
> Order groups by decreasing length of group:
>      arrange(ddply(test,.(a),mutate,key=length(a)),desc(key))[,-3]   # the
> "-3" for removing the temp key column is particularly ugly

I don't think I see any easy way of doing this using existing plyr
functions. But I'd implement as follows:

pieces <- dlply(mtcars, "cyl")
summary <- ldply(pieces, nrow)
rbind.fill(pieces[order(summary$V1)])

summary <- ldply(pieces, summarise, V1 = mean(mpg))
rbind.fill(pieces[order(summary$V1)])

That has something of a flavour of reorder to it - not sure what I'd
call the general pattern.

> Select groups with an odd size (like 'having' in SQL):
>      ddply(test,.(a),function(d) if (nrow(d)%%2 == 1) d)

From above, that would be

summary <- ldply(pieces, nrow)
rbind.fill(pieces[summary$V1 %%2 == 1])

You could do this one with a new function:

filter_df <- function(it, condition) {
conditionq <- substitute(condition)
x <- eval(conditionq)
stopifnot(length(x) == 1)
if (x) it
}

But you need to introduce a pronoun:

filter_df(mtcars, nrow(it) > 100)
filter_df(mtcars, nrow(it) > 4)

ddply(mtcars, "cyl", filter_df, nrow(it) > 10)
